tasks.title: Public-facing docs: vision, architecture, ADR log, CONTRIBUTING
tasks.description: Write the public renditions that a visitor to the repo needs: docs/vision.md, docs/architecture.md, the first ADRs recording decisions already made (single-HTML source, no ZIP container, no arbitrary script in the native profile, toolchain), and a brief CONTRIBUTING.md. These are condensed public documents derived from the plan/docs/ design pack, not copies of it. Also define the conformance programme that TRADEMARKS.md defers, so that claims of FRWD compatibility have a published, testable standard behind them, and decide whether to promote the normative format spec into spec/FRWD-0.1.md at that point.

tasks.title: apps/editor - minimal flowing edit surface
tasks.description: The MVP editor slice, after the t-024 ADR settles the architecture. Modest on purpose: open a real .frwd, render with its own document CSS, directly edit ordinary text, basic inline bold/italic/link, insert a paragraph, preserve and mint stable ids correctly, select and move one semantic block such as a figure, change a theme token, undo and redo, save .frwd, publish .frwd.html. No AI panel - t-023 already defines the seam it plugs into later. Engine choice for this slice: bare ProseMirror scoped to one block - an implementation choice, not a FRWD dependency. Region schema stays narrow: text, strong, emphasis, link, hard break, and an opaque inline atom that preserves valid inline content the region editor does not understand (inline MathML, unknown inline elements) as uneditable-but-preserved rather than normalising it away. If the view mounts on the real FRWD block element, everything it adds is editor chrome and must not survive commit. Paste crosses the same trust boundary as any other import and goes through the safety profile. Region history is transient and local; the durable undo model belongs to the editor, with a whole region edit committing as one entry alongside FRWD Ops.

tasks.title: Agent integration boundary and editor architecture reconciliation
tasks.description: Documentation only. Records the durable AI architecture now that the operations write surface is complete enough to describe it without speculation: AI reads through FRWD document tools and writes through FRWD Ops, and the model or agent host is replaceable and not part of the document format. Adds a section to 06_AI_NATIVE_EDITING_PROTOCOL.md covering that AI is external to the document (a .frwd carries no credentials, keys, chat history, agent state, model configuration or required AI runtime), the preferred write path through preview and prepared commit, the agent-facing read surface including render_document as an agent capability rather than a format requirement, that whole-document generation stays valid for initial creation but must clear the same parser, structural validation and safety profile, and that agent hosts - built-in AI, MCP, CLI or SDK, external coding agents, local models, enterprise hosts - are adapters and none of them is normative. Also reconciles 07_EDITOR_ARCHITECTURE.md with decisions since made: the load pipeline inspects rather than sanitizes, so opening an unsafe document never silently mutates it; stable ids are preserved throughout editing rather than restored on save; and React and a ProseMirror or Tiptap class engine are candidates rather than recommendations, with the choice left to the t-023 successor ADR in t-010. Does not choose or implement MCP, PTY integration, model APIs or the AI panel.

tasks.title: Editor architecture spike and ADR: who owns the FRWD document model
tasks.description: Answer one question with evidence before any editor is built: does the structured editing engine own the whole FRWD document model, or does it edit rich-text regions while the validated FRWD DOM stays authoritative? FRWD canonical form is semantic HTML; ProseMirror deliberately uses its own schema-constrained representation and Tiptap documents warn that non-conforming HTML can be lost. FRWD carries arbitrary section structure, stable ids, inline and display MathML, SVG, tables, frwd-* custom elements, inert dataset blocks, document-defined classes and attributes, and embedded media - so the distinction is real rather than theoretical. Run an adversarial round-trip spike using the business report, rich manual and scientific paper: parse into a structured-editor document model and serialize back with no edit, then measure what survives. Record the result as an ADR covering approach A (whole-document structured model) versus approach B (FRWD-DOM-native with structured rich-text regions), and how human fine-grained editing transactions meet FRWD semantic transactions without creating two durable document models.
